note:
The live-model gate (EVAL-2, ADR-0046 decision 12). `make eval-extraction-live` runs the same corpus in evals/fixtures/extraction/ through a real extractor instead of the rule-based one, and reports into the same axes as evals/baseline.json against this file instead of that one — because deterministic and live numbers are not comparable, and one file holding both would invite exactly that comparison.

Every axis here is deliberately UNBOUNDED, so this run reports and does not gate. That is not an oversight and it is not a permanent state: no number has been measured on this path yet, and ADR-0046 decision 13's discipline is that a floor invented before a measurement is a wish. The first live run writes them — read the report, then set the floors here with `slack` the way evals/baseline.json does.

Two things to know before setting them. (1) The number that actually matters on this path is hallucination_rate: a rule-based extractor copies spans and cannot invent, which is why the deterministic baseline gates it at zero by construction, and a model genuinely can — so this is the one axis where the live run is measuring something the nightly structurally cannot. Do not copy the deterministic `max: 0.0` here without deciding you mean it. (2) The scenario axes (accuracy, recall, abstention, knowledge_update) are absolutes in the deterministic baseline because a ruleset's output is predictable; a model summarises, so a scenario's marker phrase may legitimately not survive extraction. Re-read those before bounding them here, rather than assuming they carry over.

Key the floors to the model that produced them. The report's `extracted by:` line and each group's `model_versions` carry what the API actually served, taken from the record's own provenance rather than from the alias the request asked for — so a baseline set against one model and run against another is visible in the report instead of silent.
